facts.fact: On 18 March 2025 armed police stormed the Risaala Media station in Mogadishu, took it off-air and arrested five named journalists without a court warrant, after it was first to report the bombing of the president's convoy; the document gives no law.

On 18 March 2025 Mogadishu police rounded up 19 journalists who came to report on the bombing of the president's convoy, took them to Hamar Jajab police station, confiscated their equipment and deleted their footage before releasing them.

facts.fact: Geeska Freedom Centre reports that police arrested journalist Abdukadir Abukar Ali on 25 June 2026 after he published a video questioning the fairness of a trial, accusing him of insulting judicial institutions; he was bailed on 28 June with charges pending.

Geeska Freedom Centre reports that police arrested Iftiimiye TV reporter Mohamed Ali Mohamud on 26 June 2026 after he reported a police officer's claim that senior officers had unlawfully suspended his salary, and held him three days without charge.

Geeska Freedom Centre reports that NISA officers forcibly disappeared Xogbile founder Mascuud Warsame on 30 June 2026, an outlet that has published reporting critical of the South West State administration, and that he remained in custody without charge.

note: The 28 June arrests of ten influencers were for alleged indecent content, not speech about the government.

facts.fact: WardheerNews states that on 2 March 2025 access to its own site was blocked on Hormuud Telecommunications' network across Mogadishu, Hirshabelle, Galmudug, South West State and Jubaland, which it attributes to the government.
WardheerNews states that political commentator and journalist Ali Adan Mumin was arrested on 1 March 2025 on charges of threatening national security and defaming government officials.

RSF reports that the National Union of Somali Journalists, through its Secretary General, criticised the draft Penal Code adopted by the Council of Ministers in December 2025 as risking a more restrictive environment for independent journalism and drawn up without meaningful consultation.

note: The draft code's speech offences are not law and no one is reported charged under them.
